newsitem.title: HAITI: Crowd attacks Haitian police station after killing.
newsitem.headline: Crowd attacks Haitian police station after killing.

text.p: About 300 people attacked a police station on the Haitian island of La Gonave after a police officer shot and killed a man he was arresting, a U.N. spokesman said on Tuesday.
The crowd surrounded the Anse a Galets police station, hurled rocks and set the station and courthouse on fire.

Seven policemen were in the station when the attack began at about 8 p.m. on Monday (0100 Tuesday) but there were no reports of casualties, said Eric Falt, spokesman for the U.N. peacekeeping mission in Haiti.
A crowd of people milled around the scene on Tuesday morning but the situation had calmed, Falt said.
"We sent in a helicopter with five Civpol (U.N. civilian police trainers) to solve the situation peacefully," he said.
The fire seriously damaged the courthouse but the police station was relatively unscathed, Falt said.
The names of the police officer and the man he killed were not available.

The Haitian National Police is a young, inexperienced force trained over the past year by foreign police teams to replace the army, which was disbanded by former president Jean-Bertrand Aristide in 1995.
